items.company: ISU Specialty Chemical and Ares Materials
items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The companies said performance data and models generated while developing the first material would carry forward into later generations, so each could start from an existing performance model rather than from scratch.
items.signal: A co-development agreement combines ISU’s specialty-chemical and lithium-sulfide manufacturing with Ares’ AI formulation framework, which is to be tuned using cell-level battery test data. The planned carryover of device-level data and models is a potential distinctive data asset; no measured operating benefit is reported yet.
items.source: Yahoo Finance, carrying a PRNewswire release

items.quantitative_outcome: “under three months” to deliver an industrial-grade cosmetic active compound for SHINEHIGH Innovation. The announcement also says the approach compressed a process that traditionally unfolds over years “into a matter of months.”
items.signal: The company reports an industrial delivery using generative molecular modeling and automated physical-lab verification. This is a stated timeline outcome, but the source gives no specific baseline duration, independent validation, or details sufficient to assess how difficult the result would be for competitors to reproduce.
items.source: Deep Principle announcement distributed by EZ Newswire and carried by Fortune

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The release says the companies demonstrated that quantum algorithms can accurately model key properties of EUV photoresist materials; it reports no numerical accuracy or comparison result.
items.signal: The collaboration has produced a reported demonstration focused on semiconductor photoresists and is developing an FTQC-ready software pipeline. This is a relevant materials capability and partnership, but the release does not quantify an advantage or identify the comparison used.

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The company announced development of an AI platform drawing on its accumulated scientific knowledge and industrial experience; it reported no measured outcome or existing dataset scale.
items.signal: The proposed platform would combine AI with SMX’s knowledge of molecular marking, materials, and industrial processes in a scientific-intelligence environment. This is a possible proprietary-data signal, but the platform is still in development and the announcement does not substantiate the dataset’s distinctiveness or any operating benefit.
items.source: SMX announcement distributed by ACCESS Newswire and carried by Yahoo Finance

items.quantitative_outcome: The companies announced a planned dataset combining 100 million single-cell RNA-seq profiles with more than 11,000 proteomic secretome profiles, covering over 150,000 individual and combinatorial cytokine and drug perturbation conditions. No measured operating benefit is stated.
items.signal: Planned creation of a large multimodal, perturbation dataset for immune biology, with named pharma and biotech foundational partners. This is a distinctive data-access move, but the announcement describes a dataset being generated, not a demonstrated advantage.
items.source: Company announcement carried by Business Wire

items.company: Eli Lilly and Alzheimer’s Drug Discovery Foundation (ADDF)
items.quantitative_outcome: The SpeechDx resource follows more than 2,000 participants over three years. No measured operating benefit is stated.
items.signal: Lilly licensed a longitudinal speech-and-biomarker dataset for Alzheimer’s research. The dataset’s participant count and duration are stated; the source does not report a measured AI benefit or performance result.
items.source: ADDF announcement, as reported by Unite.AI

items.comparator: The article says analysis time fell from approximately nine months to 90 hours; it does not identify a separate baseline method beyond that comparison.
items.quantitative_outcome: “The AI-assisted approach reduced analysis time from approximately nine months to 90 hours and uncovered 99 vulnerabilities, including 66 that were previously unknown.” The release also states: “The total cost of the automated static analysis was just $935, averaging just $2.58 per finding.”
items.signal: AI-assisted vulnerability research produced a large reported reduction in analysis time and a quantified discovery yield across 10 TCP/IP stacks. This is a weak competitive-advantage signal: the work used off-the-shelf AI, and the report describes a specialized research harness, but does not establish that the outcome is difficult for competitors to reproduce.
items.source: Forescout Technologies / Vedere Labs, “Finding Critical Infrastructure Bugs with Off-the-Shelf AI” (reported in company announcement).

items.comparator: Rolling-force prediction hit rate: 88% before, 98% after. Metallographic inspection: 10 minutes per sample before, 3–5 minutes after. The source gives no baseline for the two-hour blast-furnace temperature forecast (>90% accuracy).
items.quantitative_outcome: The source reports: “The rolling-force prediction hit rate rose from 88% to 98%” and “inspection of a steel sample fell from 10 minutes to 3–5 minutes.” It also reports that “blast-furnace temperature forecasts two hours ahead are right over 90% of the time.”
items.signal: NISCO and Huawei reported AI deployment across NISCO plants, including more than 300 models and 25 business agents. The prediction and inspection improvements are measured operating benefits; the source notes the companies did not explain the method for calculating the broader annual cost savings, so those are not included here.
items.source: Case-studies.ai, summarizing NISCO and Huawei company releases

items.comparator: The validation figures are reported as outcomes; the source does not state a before-and-after baseline or comparator for anomaly detection, downtime, or labor time. Its separate inference benchmark compares 9.54 seconds with 3.28 seconds.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report says the solution “achieved over 90% anomaly detection accuracy, reduced unplanned downtime by up to 30%, and cut maintenance labor time by up to 50%.” For a separate 2K-input inference benchmark, end-to-end latency “decreased from 9.54 seconds to 3.28 seconds.”
items.signal: Reported industrial maintenance validation results are potentially useful operating benefits, but the source does not give the validation setup, baseline, or measurement period for the downtime and labor claims. The inference result is a benchmark, not evidence of a plant operating gain.
items.source: Yonhap News Agency, carrying a PRNewswire release
